decisions: S-curve is an explainable logistic approximation fitted with a standard-library logit linear regression over zero-based period indexes.
The carrying capacity is conservatively above the observed maximum by an explicit configurable margin; lower bound is the observed minimum.
Insufficient, constant, declining or non-monotonic series return no fit instead of manufacturing a growth curve.
Prediction clamps exponent calculation for numerical safety and uses nextafter to remain strictly inside the asymptote when floating-point rounding would equal the capacity.
No external numerical dependency or provider integration was introduced.
risks: The approximation assumes equally spaced periods and monotonic growth; irregular dates and substitution curves require later modeling.
A capacity based on the observed range is a heuristic, not a domain-calibrated forecast.
